meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'trash bin' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: С одной вашей мусоркой я справился.
examples.trans: I handled one of your trash bins.

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

справиться.gloss: to manage, to cope, to handle

meanings.note: often + с + instrumental, or used absolutely

examples.text: Мы за два года тут не справимся.
examples.trans: We won't manage here in two years.

examples.text: Конечно, не справитесь. Вы же не я.
examples.trans: Of course you won't manage. You're not me, after all.

examples.text: Мы обязательно справимся и с этим.
examples.trans: We will definitely cope with this too.
All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.text: Главное в нашем деле — умение работать с документами.
examples.trans: The main thing in our work is knowing how to work with documents.

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'тверждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to confirm', paired with 'подтвердить'.

examples.trans: Do you confirm this, Ivan Vasilyevich?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'права'). Common feminine noun meaning 'district office' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is the plan from the district office.

examples.text: Ты же глава управления, а женщину боишься.
examples.trans: You're the head of the department, and you're afraid of a woman.
A garbage bin on the street.

examples.text: Отнеси скорее в мусорный бак на улицу.
examples.trans: Take it quickly to the garbage bin outside.

examples.text: Баки должны стоять именно в этом месте.
examples.trans: The bins must stand exactly in this place.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to supply'.

examples.text: Тимур? Ты решил поставлять ей продукты?
examples.trans: Timur? You decided to supply her with food?

examples.text: Это слово «поставлять» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to supply' is often heard in conversation.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'дукт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'product, foodstuff' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты будешь целый день разгружать продукты!
examples.trans: You will unload groceries the whole day!
The guests need the freshest product!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чтение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'respect' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «почтение» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'respect' is often heard in conversation.

учесть.gloss: to take into account, to consider

meanings.en: to take into account, to factor in
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'честь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take into account, to consider', paired with 'учитывать'.

examples.trans: The court considered the new circumstances.
The court has considered the new circumstances of the case.

meanings.note: в долгу не остаться = to repay a favour

examples.text: Помогите мне! Я в долгу не останусь.
examples.trans: Help me! I'll pay you back, I promise.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'отрудничество'). Common neuter noun meaning 'cooperation' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Извините, наше сотрудничество подошло к концу.
examples.trans: Excuse me, our cooperation has come to an end.

examples.text: Это слово «сотрудничество» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'cooperation' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'чить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to contradict'.

examples.trans: I cannot contradict an older man.

examples.text: Это слово «перечить» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to contradict' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: higher in age or class rank

examples.trans: All the upper grades are going tomorrow.
I cannot contradict an older man.
We need a more objective assessment.

examples.text: Погоди, нам нужна более объективная оценка.
examples.trans: Wait, we need a more objective opinion.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Да я три года грузчиком работал. Тут дел на пятнадцать минут.
examples.trans: Oh, I worked as a mover for three years. This is fifteen minutes' work.

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: followed by the genitive plural: 'десять минут'

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.
